result.rationale: The diff adds `refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token = "refresh_token";` in parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts. Callers like zoomvideo and office365 pass the raw provider response (which commonly omits refresh_token on rotation per RFC), so the sentinel literal is written into the stored credential key, and the next local refresh call would submit 'refresh_token' as the credential. Also, when APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED the code stores this parsed data back to prisma.credential.update in the Google path. The fabricated literal replacing a real token is a verifiable correctness defect introduced

judged_text: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:26 — [P1, confidence 100] Whenever a valid provider or broker response omits token rotation, `refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token = "refresh_token";` replaces the reusable stored token with a fabricated literal, so the next local-provider refresh submits an invalid credential; retaining the old token is available to callers and the sentinel cannot preserve that lifecycle.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies a bug in parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts at lines 24-26. When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is false (local provider path), if the response doesn't contain a refresh_token, the code sets `refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token = "refresh_token"` - a literal string. This fabricated token will be stored in the database and used for the next refresh attempt, which will fail because "refresh_token" is not a valid token. The function should preserve the original refresh_token from the credential rather than inserting a placeholder string. This is a real correctness bug that would cause token refresh failures.
